_comment: A team's LAST unit routs, without instantly losing. Stages team 0's ONLY unit -- a full-strength (120) but shaken (morale 10) player infantry -- meeting a single, slightly larger enemy infantry (130) head-on. Both blocks are pinned to Tight (formation 1) so packed files still produce the rout inside this clip. Sustained frontal casualties and being outnumbered (the local force ratio, 120 to 130) erode its morale to 0 (#529), and it breaks and flees (faded) while barely bloodied. It used to trigger instant defeat + a paused freeze the moment its last fightable unit left the line; now the battle stays live while it's routing. Routing units are still valid combat targets, and the enemy follows it in its ranks as it flees. Each routed man runs on his own from the enemy he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), and the unit's position is the centroid of its men. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-14 on #1949's branch: it breaks at tick 1192, 1120, 1192, 782 and 976, and at tick 1300, the clip's end, every seed is ROUTING and out of contact. The pins are seed-robust: FIGHTING at tick 750, ROUTING at ticks 1200 and 1300, and out of contact at tick 1300. They replace pins that held on the clip's own seed only: FIGHTING at tick 950, ROUTING at tick 1000 and the position (655.4, 270.13), tol 5 wu, at tick 1300, read when seed 0 broke at tick 976 (on main c36560fa those pins failed on seeds 1 to 4). This grind's breaking tick swings with any change to how the men of the two blocks press: when a pair of men walking back to their places took the contact band (#1949), seed 0 broke at tick 1192 instead of 976. STAGING (#1827): blocks front to front now meet at their front ranks, so only the front ranks trade blows, and against an equal 120 it no longer broke reliably inside the clip. This clip only needs to show the rout starting and the battle staying live through it, not the whole grind. No player input needed.

follow_error.reason: follow_error, the relational successor of shape_residual, reads uid1 24.55 against 6.75 on this tree (dense 2-tick FULL dump, Windows, seed 0, measured 2026-11-13); the slot-based shape_residual this exemption was written against read uid1 22.9. Original reason: The pursuer (uid 1) chases the router with its grid still scrambled from the fight: its slot residual reads 12 to 16 wu while in contact (not judged) and 19 to 21 wu once contact breaks, against 6.75. Measured 2026-11-10 on aef5b476, seeds 0 to 4. On dense 2-tick FULL dumps over ticks 2 to 1400, every exemption removed, the verdict FAILS on seeds 0, 1, 3 and 4 (worst 22.9, 27.2, 38 and 24.2) and passes on seed 2 (0.00171). On the clip's own declared ticks (950, 1000, 1300) it passes on every seed (worst 0), so there the exemption reads STALE. Kept because it fires on four of five seeds on dense dumps. The same deformation in pursuit reads 25.2 on merge-base a3714751's own staging (2-tick samples), where it does not last long enough to fail the check; this staging breaks earlier (#1827). #1824 tracks a pursuer deforming at the edge of a router's contact range.
